max.description: Most machines: a number, or a range each deployment picks from.

min.description: Fewest machines: a number, or a range each deployment picks from.

Build.description: How to build a daemon from source.

binary-name.description: Name of the binary to build (rust, required; typescript, defaults to the package name).

command.description: Process argv that starts the application (python, required).

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile path relative to `src` (docker). Defaults to "Dockerfile".

package.description: Workspace package to install (python). Omit for a single-package project.

python-version.description: Python version of the runtime image (python). Defaults to 3.12.

src.description: Source directory, relative to where `alien` runs. Defaults to ".".

toolchain.description: Which build to run: "rust", "typescript", "python" or "docker". Go and other languages use "docker".

Choice.description: A count: one number, or a range a deployment picks from.

ChoiceRange.description: A range a deployment picks from; `default` applies when it does not pick.

allowed.description: The fewest and the most the deployer may choose, `[min, max]`.

default.description: Used when the deployer does not choose.

Cpu.description: CPU cores: a number such as 2 or 0.5, or a quantity string such as "500m".

Daemon.description: A daemon: a long-running process on every machine of its pool.

build.description: Build the daemon from source, for example `{ toolchain = "rust", binary-name = "acme-agent" }`. Set this or `image`.

command.description: Command to run instead of the image's default.

cpu.description: CPU cores reserved for the daemon. Defaults to 0.1.

enabled-when.description: Create this daemon only when this deployer-provided boolean `[input.<id>]` is true.

env.description: Environment variables: literal values, or `{ input = "<id>" }` to take the value of a stack input. These win over `env-file`.

env-file.description: One file, or a list of files, of `KEY=value` lines, relative to alien.toml, read when the stack is loaded. Later files win over earlier ones.

host-access.description: Full access to the host: privileged, the host's PID namespace and network, the host's `/` mounted at `/host`, running as root (uid 0).

image.description: Run a prebuilt container image. Set this or `build`.

lifecycle.description: Who owns the daemon after setup. Defaults to "live" (each release updates it).

links.description: Resources this daemon uses, by ID.

memory.description: Memory reserved for the daemon, for example "4Gi". Defaults to "128Mi".

permissions.description: Gives the daemon a cloud identity: the name of a `[permissions.<name>]` profile, or the grants themselves, `{ <resource-id> = ["storage/data-read"] }`, which make a profile named after the daemon. Omit for none. On AWS, GCP and Azure it cannot be combined with `host-access`.

pool.description: Pool to run on. Omit to run on every pool.

runtime.description: Container runtime settings for anything between the defaults and `host-access`, for example `{ network-mode = "host" }` to bind the daemon's ports on the machine itself. Cannot be combined with `host-access`.

stop-grace-period.description: How long the daemon may take to stop on updates, drains and deletes: seconds, or a duration such as "10m" or "24h". At most 24 hours.

DataDisk.description: A data disk size: one size, or a range a deployment picks from.

DataDiskRange.description: Data disk sizes a deployment picks from, as quantities such as "50Gi" or "1Ti".

allowed.description: The smallest and the largest size the deployer may choose, `[min, max]`.

default.description: Used when the deployer does not choose.

Duration.description: A duration: whole seconds, or a string such as "90s", "10m" or "24h".

host-label.description: Host label under the deployment's domain. "@" is the domain itself. Defaults to the endpoint name.

wildcard-subdomains.description: Also route every subdomain of the host label.

EnvMapping.description: An environment variable for chosen resources.

target-resources.description: IDs of the resources that get it. A trailing `*` matches a prefix.

anyOf.description: The variable name; every daemon gets it.
The variable name and the resources that get it.

EnvTarget.description: An environment variable that receives an input's value.

anyOf.description: A literal. Numbers and booleans are written as their text.
The value of a stack input, set when the deployment is created.

EnvValue.description: One environment variable of a workload.

EnvVarType.description: How an input's value reaches the environment.

failure-threshold.description: Consecutive failures before the daemon counts as unhealthy. Defaults to 3.

timeout.description: How long one check may take: seconds, or a duration such as "2s". Defaults to 1 second.

Input.description: A stack input: a value provided per deployment. Its ID is the table name.

default.description: Value used when none is provided.

description.description: What the value is for. Required for required inputs.

env.description: Environment variables that receive the value: a name, `{ name, target-resources }`, or a list. Without `target-resources` every daemon gets it.

kind.description: What kind of value it is.

label.description: Shown where the value is asked for. Defaults to the input ID.

max.description: Largest accepted number (number and integer inputs).

max-length.description: Longest accepted string (string and secret inputs).

min.description: Smallest accepted number (number and integer inputs).

min-length.description: Shortest accepted string (string and secret inputs).

pattern.description: Regular expression the value must match (string and secret inputs).

placeholder.description: Example shown in an empty field.

platforms.description: Ask for the input only on these platforms.

provided-by.description: Who provides the value: "developer", "deployer", or both. Defaults to "developer".

required.description: Whether a deployment needs a value. Defaults to true.

InputKind.description: The kind of value an input takes.

InputReference.description: `{ input = "<id>" }`: the variable takes the value of a stack input.

type.description: Whether the variable is "plain" or a "secret". Defaults from the input's kind.

InputValue.description: A value as written in TOML: string, number, boolean, or list of strings.

Mount.description: A host path mounted into a daemon.

OneOrMany_for_EnvTarget.description: One value or a list of them.

OneOrMany_for_Provider.description: One value or a list of them.

OneOrMany_for_String.description: One value or a list of them.

anyOf.description: Grants per resource ID; they make a profile named after the workload.

Permissions.description: A workload's permissions: a profile by name, or the grants themselves.

Pool.description: A machine pool. On machines deployments the pool name is what `join --capacity-group` takes.

autoscaling.description: Scale between a minimum and a maximum number of machines. Set this or `machines`.

cpu.description: CPU cores each machine needs, for example 4.

data-disk.description: An extra empty block device each machine must provide: one size such as "1Ti", or a range each deployment picks from, `{ default = "200Gi", allowed = ["0Gi", "4Ti"] }`.

ephemeral-storage.description: Size of the disk holding the operating system. Defaults to "20Gi".

failure-domain-spread.description: How many failure domains (zones) the pool's machines spread across, 1 to 255.

machines.description: A fixed number of machines: `2`, or a range each deployment picks from, `{ default = 2, allowed = [1, 5] }`. Set this or `autoscaling`.

memory.description: Memory each machine needs, for example "16Gi".

nested-virtualization.description: Whether machines must support nested virtualization (to run VMs inside them).

ResourceLifecycle.description: Describes the lifecycle of a resource within a stack, determining how it's managed and deployed.

oneOf.description: Frozen resources are owned by setup. Setup creates, updates, and deletes them. Alien may heartbeat them and may run explicit management operations when setup granted management permissions.
Live resources are owned by Alien. Alien creates, updates, deletes, and replaces them after setup, so Live resources require provision permissions.

Runtime.description: Container runtime settings of a daemon.

mounts.description: Host paths mounted into the container.

network-mode.description: "host" binds the daemon's ports on the machine itself, so `localhost:<port>` on the server reaches it. "appnet" is the default container network.

pid-namespace.description: "host" shares the machine's process namespace, "private" is the default.

user.description: Numeric uid, or uid:gid, to run as.

enabled-when.description: Create this bucket only when this deployer-provided boolean `[input.<id>]` is true.

lifecycle.description: Who owns the bucket. Defaults to "frozen" (setup creates it).

public-read.description: Allow anyone to read objects without credentials.

versioning.description: Keep previous versions of overwritten objects.

oneOf.description: Cargo builds a binary, cross-compiled for the target machines.
Bun compiles the project to a single executable.

description:
A stack written as `alien.toml`.

It describes the same resources as an `alien.ts` file and resolves to the same stack.

cluster.description: ID of the compute cluster that holds the pools. Defaults to "compute". Set it when moving an existing stack to alien.toml so its cluster keeps its ID.

daemon.description: Daemons: one process on every machine of their pool.

input.description: Stack inputs: values provided per deployment, by the developer or the deployer.

name.description: Stack name. Letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, up to 128 characters.

permissions.description: Permission profiles, by name. Each maps a resource ID (or "*" for every resource) to the permission sets granted on it, such as `["storage/data-read"]`.

platforms.description: Platforms this stack can be deployed to. Omit to allow every platform.

pool.description: Machine pools: what hardware each pool's machines need and how many run.

title: alien.toml
